---
title: "omero-screen-images CLI"
---

::: {.callout-note}
This page covers what the tool is for and how it is used. For every option,
its default and its type, run `omero-screen-images <command> --help`: the help
text is generated from the code, so it is always current.
:::

## What this tool does

`omero-screen-images` renders the images the napari widgets produce, without
opening napari, so a script, a notebook or an agent can regenerate them
reproducibly:

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `gallery` | A grid of cell crops per well, optionally one classifier class or an explicit cell selection |
| `well` | A whole-well overview: stitched multichannel composite with a caption and scale bar, the whole well or zoomed in 2x steps |
| `batch` | Everything listed in a plan file, one run per plate and render |

Each run writes a JSON manifest next to the images (`gallery_export.json`,
`well_overview.json`, `batch.json`). It records the version, the settings, the
seed, the display limits and the outcome for every well, so a panel can be
traced and replayed months later. Add `--json` to also print the manifest:
stdout then carries only the manifest and the logs go to stderr, so the output
can be piped straight into a parser.

`omero-screen-images` is installed with `omero-screen-napari`. Like the other
CLIs it reads the `.env.{name}` configuration; choose it with `--env` before the
command:

```bash
omero-screen-images --env production gallery 5108 --wells G5 --channels DAPI
```

## Where the pixels come from

- **Plates with a zarr cache** (stitched plates cached from the plate-info
  dialog) are read lazily from the cache. Nothing is downloaded.
- **Per-field plates** are loaded through the plate disk cache, downloading from
  OMERO on a miss, one well at a time to bound memory. Overviews are stitched in
  memory from the stage positions with the plate's per-objective stitch
  calibration, as in the welldata widget.
- A stitched plate without a zarr cache is refused: build the cache first.

Galleries also need the plate's measurements in CellView; overviews do not.

## Display limits

Every well of one call shares one set of display limits, so wells rendered
together can be compared side by side. By default these are the
0.1/99.9 percentiles pooled over the requested wells (exact zeros, i.e. canvas
no field covers, are ignored). The same call always gives the same limits,
whatever the order of the wells.

To compare across calls, or to match an earlier figure, fix them with
`--limits CHANNEL=LO:HI` (repeatable). The limits used, and whether each was
given or pooled, are in the manifest.

## Galleries

```bash
# 5x5 DAPI crops of micronucleated cells in two wells
omero-screen-images --env production gallery 5108 --wells E2,G5 \
    --classifier-column classifier_nuclei4 --class micronuclei \
    --channels DAPI --grid 5x5 --seed 1 --out qc/micronuclei
```

- `--channels` packs up to three channels into R, G, B. One channel gives the
  inverted greyscale gallery.
- `--classifier-column` / `--class` keep one class of one classifier column.
  Naming the column avoids the widget's fallback (the first classifier column
  that contains the value).
- `--seed` fixes the draw: the same command reproduces the same gallery, and
  each well draws independently.
- The background around each cell is **kept** by default. `--blank-background`
  blanks everything outside the cell's mask; that hides objects outside the
  mask, such as micronuclei, and makes crops look processed.

### Galleries from an analysis gate

`--cells cells.csv` (or `.parquet`) restricts the draw to cells chosen
downstream, for example EdU-negative 2N cells gated in a CellView analysis. The
table needs `image_id` and `label` (the CellView nucleus label), and optionally
`timepoint`; the wells are taken from the selection when `--wells` is omitted.

```python
gate = df.filter(...)  # a CellView export, filtered in a notebook
gate.select("image_id", "label").write_csv("gate.csv")
```

```bash
omero-screen-images gallery 5108 --cells gate.csv --channels DAPI,EdU --json
```

## Whole-well overviews

```bash
# Every channel of four wells, same contrast for all four
omero-screen-images --env production well 5108 --wells B2,E2,B5,E5 --out qc/wells

# DAPI with nuclei outlines, zoomed 8x into the upper left of the well
omero-screen-images well 5108 --wells G5 --layers DAPI,nuclei_masks \
    --zoom 8 --center 0.3,0.3
```

- `--layers` lists what to draw: channel names plus `nuclei_masks` and
  `cell_masks`, drawn as outlines. The default is every channel and no masks.
- `--zoom 1` is the whole well; each step halves the field of view around
  `--center Y,X` (fractions of the well height and width).
- The image is read at the resolution closest to `--size` (default 2000 px on
  the longer side) and downsampled by averaging, so it is not aliased.
- Channels keep their napari colours whichever subset is drawn. The caption
  carries the plate, well and all the well's metadata.

## Batches

A plan is a CSV with one row per image:

```text
plate_id,well,render
5108,B2,well
5108,G5,well
5108,G5,gallery:micronuclei
5108,E2,gallery:normal
```

`render` is `well`, `gallery`, or `gallery:<class>` (a class of
`--classifier-column`).

```bash
omero-screen-images --env production batch plan.csv \
    --channels DAPI --classifier-column classifier_nuclei4 --out qc/
```

Rows with the same plate and render are rendered together, so they share
display limits, into `qc/<plate>_<render>/` with their own manifest;
`qc/batch.json` lists every run. The options apply to every row. A plate that
fails is recorded in the batch manifest and the rest of the plan still runs.
